issue.title: A wrong APP_CONFIG path is silently ignored
issue.body:
We run our own instance with `APP_CONFIG=/etc/ledgerline/app.yml`. The file we
deploy is actually called `app.yaml`, so the path pointed at nothing, and the
service started normally on the built-in defaults: two import loops instead of
our eight, the default poll interval, and nothing in the logs about it. It took
us two days to notice. The configuration reference says values come from the
file named by APP_CONFIG; starting without a word when that file doesn't exist
seems wrong.

input.title: Fail loudly when APP_CONFIG points at a missing file
input.body:
File: src/config.ts

In readFileConfig, `if (!fs.existsSync(file)) return {};` also swallows a missing file when APP_CONFIG is explicitly set. Change it so that a missing file is still tolerated for the default config/app.yaml path (when APP_CONFIG is unset), but throws a clear error such as `APP_CONFIG file not found: <path>` when APP_CONFIG is set and the file doesn't exist. A typo like app.yml then stops startup instead of silently using defaults.
